themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints spiked to 15 THIS WEEK versus a baseline average of 7.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 90% increase—suggesting a coordinated or environmental trigger requiring immediate investigation into hotspot locations and enforcement gaps.
evidence: 15 illegal dumping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.9 weekly average over 8-week baseline (90% spike, z-score 3.01)
Spike is concentrated in the most recent reporting period with no prior warning trend
Statistically significant deviation suggests acute, addressable problem rather than chronic condition
reporting_angles: Map the 15 complaints this week to identify if dumping is concentrated in specific neighborhoods or near transit hubs; interview Sanitation Department about enforcement response
Talk to residents and local business owners about whether they've noticed increased dumping activity and whether it correlates with construction or seasonal factors

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Spike
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.5 per week—an 700% spike with z-score 4.95—a sharp emerging problem in shared micro-mobility infrastructure that may signal theft rings, abandonment patterns, or vendor accountability issues.
evidence: 4 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 4.95, severity high)
Extremely sharp deviation from baseline with no gradual escalation pattern
First week of sustained elevated reports suggests emerging rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Contact Citi Bike and other dockless bike vendors about service levels, theft reports, and whether they've noticed increased abandonment in Midwood this week
Interview Sanitation about how many abandoned bikes they're removing and whether there are hotspot locations (near transit, schools, commercial areas) that suggest organized abandonment or theft

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 10 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 2.9 per week over 8 weeks—a 248% increase with z-score 6.11 (highest statistical severity in dataset)—indicating either a coordinated tagging campaign or breakdown in removal enforcement.
evidence: 10 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average over 8-week baseline (248% spike, z-score 6.11—highest severity in entire dataset)
Sharp one-week spike with sustained elevation compared to historical baseline
Geographic concentration likely given rapid onset; suggests active campaign or enforcement gap
reporting_angles: Photograph and map graffiti sites from last week; interview Parks Dept. and NYPD's Gang Task Force about whether they've identified organized taggers or crews active in Midwood
Report on NYPD 70th Precinct response times for graffiti removal and compare to city average; whether Sanitation removal backlog has caused tag accumulation

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 29 LAST WEEK versus 12.2 weekly average—a 137% spike with z-score 3.98—concentrated in a district with aging multi-family housing stock, suggesting either a systemic maintenance crisis or rapid deterioration in residential building compliance.
evidence: 29 elevator complaints LAST WEEK vs. 12.2 weekly average over 8-week baseline (137% increase, z-score 3.98)
Midwood has high concentration of pre-war and mid-century apartment buildings with aging elevator infrastructure
Spike correlates with heating season and potential freeze-thaw stress on mechanical systems
reporting_angles: Interview residents in buildings with elevator outages about duration of service disruptions and impact on elderly or mobility-impaired tenants; file FOIL for HPD violations on those buildings
Report on whether elevator maintenance contractors are backlogged post-holiday; whether aging equipment in district is reaching failure threshold; cost and timeline for compliance remediation

themes_detail.label: Appliance Complaints Elevated
themes_detail.summary: Appliance-related complaints spiked to 31 TWO WEEKS AGO (from 11.2 weekly baseline—a 176% increase, z-score 4.66)—likely reflecting heating system failures in winter conditions and suggesting landlord non-compliance with heat/habitability code.
evidence: 31 appliance complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 11.2 weekly average (176% spike, z-score 4.66)
Heat/hot water remains highest-volume complaint category overall (3,342 in 90 days), with appliance spikes amplifying crisis
Winter season timing suggests heating equipment failures compounding elevated baseline demand for heat-related repairs
reporting_angles: Cross-reference appliance complaint addresses with HPD heat violation records; identify which landlords have repeat violations and whether Dept. of Buildings has issued penalties or enforcement orders

Interview tenants from buildings with sustained appliance/heat complaints about living conditions, out-of-pocket repair costs, and whether they've filed complaints with housing court or tenant advocacy groups
